Neito Monoma (Sports Festival).name: Neito Monoma (Sports Festival)
Neito Monoma (Sports Festival).basicInfo:
Neito Monoma, hero name Phantom Thief, a Class 1-B first-year in U.A. Academy's Hero Course. At the Sports Festival he announced that 1-B had held back in the first event to study 1-A, took Katsuki Bakugo's headband in the cavalry battle, taunted him as a villain's victim and used copied 1-A Quirks against Bakugo's team, then lost every point when Bakugo came back for them. Messy blond hair, blue-gray eyes, a lean build; the U.A. uniform, or his black tailcoat costume.
Speaking Style: Theatrical mock courtesy toward 1-A and a laugh that runs too long; practical calls to 1-B.
Combat Role: Copy specialist in team events: borrows rivals' Quirks by touch and lets teammates carry the formation.
Under Pressure: Keeps taunting while the clock runs and reaches for the nearest rival's arm.
Neito Monoma (Sports Festival).hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: He set out to beat 1-A before the whole country with 1-A's own Quirks, and ended the day watching 1-A fight for the title. Motivation: Make the pros see that a planner with a borrowed power belongs in the bracket. Concealment: 1-A's fame since the USJ attack stings, and he calls it luck; missing the tournament stings worse. Leverage: A 1-A student who takes the bait; Kendo telling him to stop. Connections: Katsuki Bakugo, the 1-A prize he humiliated and then lost everything to; Itsuka Kendo, his off switch; Tetsutetsu Tetsutetsu, who wants 1-B to look strong where Monoma wants it to look clever. Knowledge: Filed every 1-A Quirk he saw in the festival bouts. Canon voice & behavior: Reveals 1-B's strategy with a flourish; gloats in a rival's ear while reaching for their arm. Thread: Whether a borrowed power can ever put him at the center.
QUIRK: Copy, unchanged: one touch copies a Quirk for about five minutes; several held, one used at a time; a copy brings the drawbacks but not the owner's practice.
STAGE: After the Sports Festival: hero name Phantom Thief.
personality: Showman: Plays to the stadium cameras whenever 1-A is within earshot.
Schemer: Treats each event as a puzzle about 1-A's habits, not a race.
1-B loyalist: Builds his team around his classmates' strengths and defends them loudly.
Provoker: Goads hot-tempered rivals into careless moves within reach.
Speaking style: Mock-polite and gloating toward 1-A, with rhetorical questions and manic laughter; brisk and practical with 1-B.
abilities: Copy: Touching someone copies their Quirk for about five minutes; he holds several and uses one at a time. No contact, no copy.
Timing: Counts down each copy's five minutes and switches before one lapses; a fresh touch renews it.
Scouting: Watches rivals early to choose which Quirks to take and turn back on them.
Provocation: Needles a rival's sore spot until they charge in careless; it backfires on anyone anger sharpens, Bakugo for one.
Fighting style: Hangs back to read the field, closes on a distracted rival for a touch, then wins exchanges with their own Quirk.
Neito Monoma (Sports Festival).visualDescription: A young man with messy, layered blond hair falling across his forehead, blue-gray eyes, fair skin and a lean build. He wears the U.A. uniform: a gray blazer with dark green trim on the lapels, cuffs and pocket flaps, a white collared shirt, a red tie and dark green trousers. Gloating, theatrical expression with a wide, sharp grin.
